description: #5057 — `undo_page_group` against a group whose own first revert changes the page scope it was enumerated from. The scope is a live `parent_id` walk (`page_blocks`), so an op belongs to whichever page its block sits under NOW, not the page it sat under when the op was made: C1's `create_block` and `set_property` enter Alpha's scope the moment C1 is moved there. `undo_page_group_inner` enumerates the whole group inside its `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` (`enumerate_undo_group_in_tx`) precisely so the list cannot shift under the reverts, and its doc-block names the failure by name — the old FE loop "sized the group once and then issued N offset-based undos that could drift if the op stream shifted mid-loop". This fixture is that scenario: reverting the move sends C1 back to Beta, at which point BOTH remaining ops leave Alpha's scope, so a re-derived list is empty and an offset-addressed second undo indexes past its end. Enumerated once, the group reverts exactly what it counted. No query steps: `properties` and `blocks` are both in the snapshot's five arrays, so the settled state is the evidence — C1 back under Beta, its property gone, and C1 itself tombstoned by the reverse of its own create. A one-page fixture cannot tell the two implementations apart, and neither can a group whose reverts do not move a block across pages — which is why every other undo fixture passes either way. `set_property` rather than `edit_block` for both members: an `EditBlockPayload` carries `prev_edit`, so a block's FIRST edit is non-reversible and would abort the whole batch with `NotFound` before the drift could show (`revert_ops_in_tx` runs the group with `skip_non_reversible = false`).
name: undo_group_scope_drift

ops.comment: C1 is born under BETA, and born from an OP carrying an `index`: a move's reverse reconstructs the prior placement from the newest earlier `move_block` / `create_block` row for that block (`find_prior_position`), and a create payload with neither `index` nor `position` is `NonReversible` rather than a guessed slot. A SEEDED block has no such row at all.
Made while C1 is still under Beta. Reversible from the start, unlike a block's first `edit_block` (an `EditBlockPayload` carries `prev_edit`).
C1 moves onto Alpha. From here Alpha's live subtree holds C1, so all three ops are in Alpha's scope — it is this move that put the two older ones there.

Three ops in Alpha's scope, so the group is three. Reverting the move (newest first) takes C1 back to Beta, and with it BOTH older ops leave Alpha's scope — an implementation that re-derives the scope per iteration then indexes a list that has shrunk to nothing, and answers one result or `NotFound` with the move already applied. Enumerated once, the group reverts all three and answers three.
ops.name: group_reverts_what_it_enumerated
